learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to condense a large text into a short, powerful paragraph that captures the author's core message without losing the meaning.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A summary must only contain the central theme and the most critical points of the original passage. Ignore minor details.
Do not include examples, statistics, quotes, or long explanations in a summary. Cut out all redundant (repetitive) information.
Never just copy and paste sentences from the original text. You must understand the meaning and rewrite it (paraphrase) using your own vocabulary.
A summary is strictly based on the author's text. Never add your own opinions, thoughts, or outside knowledge into the summary.
A standard summary should be about one-third (1/3) the length of the original passage. It must be written as a single, coherent paragraph.

fun_activity.title: 🎬 The Movie Pitch
fun_activity.instructions: Think of a 3-hour movie you watched recently. Try to tell the entire story from beginning to end in exactly 3 sentences. That is the art of summarizing!

exam_tips: 📌 A summary is usually written immediately after note-making. Use your 'Notes' to write the summary instead of reading the long passage again!
📌 Write the summary in one single paragraph. Do not use bullet points or headings.
📌 Keep an eye on the word count. If the question asks for 80 words, try to stick between 75 and 85 words.
quick_recap: ⭐ Summarising is the opposite of expanding; it is the art of compression.
⭐ Transition words (like however, therefore, moreover) help make your summary flow smoothly.
⭐ The summary must make complete sense even to someone who hasn't read the original passage.
